title: PCIe-style data link layer: TLP framing with sequence numbers and LCRC, Ack/Nak DLLPs with CRC-16, replay buffer, replay and Ack latency timers, flow control for Posted / Non-Posted / Completion header and data credits (InitFC1/InitFC2/UpdateFC), ASPM L1 entry and exit, on a PIPE-like symbol interface

fields.desc: physical link up: starts flow-control init; clearing it drops the link (buffers and sequence numbers reset)
ASPM: ask for L1 whenever the link is idle (PM_Active_State_Request_L1); a TX write wakes the link
ASPM: accept L1 requests from the far side when idle

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: TLP byte to send; one write per byte, LAST on the final byte (a TLP is cut after MAXLEN = 32 bytes). The first byte is the TLP header's {Fmt, Type}: it selects the credit type (Posted, Non-Posted, Completion) and whether data credits are used. The core takes bytes in L0 while the link is up and a replay-buffer slot is free

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Received TLP byte (head of the core's receive buffer); reading it pops it. TLPs are delivered once their LCRC and sequence number check out; header and data credits of the TLP's type are returned (UpdateFC) as its last byte is read

fields.desc: ASPM state: 0 L0, 1 requesting L1, 2 L1

irqs.name: RETRAIN
irqs.desc: the fourth replay without progress: the physical layer should retrain

irqs.name: ERR_TLP
irqs.desc: a TLP failed (bad LCRC, bad EDB, framing, sequence number ahead): a Nak is sent

irqs.name: ERR_SEQ
irqs.desc: a TLP with a sequence number ahead of the expected one

irqs.name: TLP_DUP
irqs.desc: a duplicate TLP (already received): dropped and acknowledged

irqs.name: TLP_NULL
irqs.desc: a nullified TLP (EDB with inverted LCRC): dropped silently

irqs.name: ERR_OVERFLOW
irqs.desc: a good TLP over the header or data credits advertised for its type: dropped, not acknowledged

irqs.name: ERR_PROTO
irqs.desc: a DLLP of unknown type, or an Ack/Nak with reserved bits or a sequence number never sent

irqs.name: ERR_FRAME
irqs.desc: a framing error (K symbol out of place, DLLP of the wrong length)

notes: tx_sym / tx_k and rx_sym / rx_k are the symbol interface (one 8-bit symbol per PCLK, K flag for STP FB, SDP 5C, END FD, EDB FE); they pass through unchanged.

The core parameters MAXLEN (32), TXN (4 replay slots), RXN (4 receive TLPs), REPLAY_TO (600), ACK_LAT (16), FC_GAP (32), UPD_GAP (1024) and the credits advertised (HP 2, HNP 1, HC 1 headers; DP 4, DNP 2, DC 2 data) keep their defaults.

Field layouts follow PCIe as we read it; they have not been checked against a compliant device. Not implemented: the physical layer (LTSSM, ordered sets, 8b/10b, scrambling), 128b/130b and flit mode, more than one lane, virtual channels other than VC0, credit scale factors, PM_Active_State_Nak, PCI-PM L1 / L2.
features: TLP framing: STP, 12-bit sequence number, 1..MAXLEN bytes, LCRC (CRC-32), END / EDB; nullified TLPs.
Ack / Nak DLLPs with CRC-16; Acks coalesced by an Ack latency timer (ACK_LAT), duplicates acknowledged at once.
Replay buffer of TXN TLPs, replay on Nak or the replay timer; retrain request after the fourth replay without progress.

Flow control per credit type (Posted, Non-Posted, Completion) with header and data credits: InitFC1 / InitFC2 handshake, UpdateFC as TLPs are read out and every UPD_GAP clocks, infinite credits, the PCIe modulo credit check.
Receive overflow detection per type (header and data) and a byte-room guard.
ASPM L1: PM_Active_State_Request_L1 / PM_Request_Ack in both directions, crossed requests, exit on a write, a received packet, a read, or anything owed.
Error events for bad LCRC, sequence numbers ahead, duplicates, framing, DLLP CRC and protocol errors.
sequence: Write CTRL with link_up set (aspm_ok as wanted); poll STATUS until dl_up reads 1.
Send: write TX once per byte, LAST on the final byte. Receive: on RX_AVAIL read RX until a byte with LAST.
Set pm_req to let the link enter L1 when idle (STATUS pm_state reads 2); a TX write wakes it.
On RETRAIN, retrain the physical layer (clear and set link_up).
